title: Decimals: place value and adding 0.4 + 0.25
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can read 0.25 by place value: 2 tenths and 5 hundredths in one number.
The class can rewrite 0.4 in hundredths before adding, matching the places first.

modelAnswers.question: Write 0.4 in hundredths and explain why the value does not change.
modelAnswers.answer: 0.4 = 0.40: four tenths is the same amount as forty hundredths, because ten hundredths make one tenth.

modelAnswers.question: Work out 0.4 + 0.25, showing the step where you rewrite 0.4.

commonErrors.misconception: Comparing decimals by digit count: 0.25 looks bigger than 0.4 because 25 > 4.
commonErrors.example: A learner picks 0.25 as the bigger number on the worksheet comparison question, pointing at the 25 as the larger count.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: lay the tenths bar over the hundredths square and compare the covered amounts, not the digit counts.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: 0.4 is forty hundredths and 0.25 is twenty-five hundredths, so 0.4 covers more of the whole.

commonErrors.misconception: Comparing decimals by digit count: 0.25 looks bigger than 0.4 because 25 > 4.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner defends 0.25 by saying it has more digits after the point than 0.4.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: rewrite both numbers in hundredths, then say which amount is larger and why.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: in hundredths the two amounts are forty and twenty-five, and forty hundredths is the larger amount.

nextSteps: Reteach the comparison with the bar laid over the square before any further comparison questions.
Practise rewriting one-decimal-place numbers in hundredths until matching the places is automatic.
